subject: PHI handling: BAA availability and deployment paths
content:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laurie Martin <laurie.martin@medsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PHI handling: BAA availability and deployment paths

Hi Laurie / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on your transcript retention and clinical review workflows. As promised, here’s a concise recap of what we discussed and the recommended next steps so your security and procurement teams can evaluate options quickly.

Summary (short):
- BAA: Redwood can execute a Business Associate Agreement for HIPAA-covered PHI for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). For Hosted (multi-tenant) we generally do not accept unrestricted PHI ingestion; we can discuss narrow exceptions but recommend Dedicated/Private for primary PHI workloads.
- PHI boundaries: Chat transcripts, uploader attachments, and any PII embedded in prompts are considered PHI in scope. We recommend token-level redaction or client-side pseudonymization for any data flowing through Hosted endpoints.
- Eligible service models:
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): full BAA coverage, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit log forwarding — recommended for regulated clinical data.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): BAA available, strong isolation, configurable audit retention; supports customer-managed keys for certain cloud integrations.
  - Hosted (public API): only for non-PHI or if you can enforce strict client-side de-identification; not the default path for PHI.

Attachments I’m dropping here for your review: Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2026.pdf (top-level controls), BAA_Draft_Redwood.docx (starter template), deployment_matrix.csv (short matrix comparing options).

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) Please confirm that the scope you expect Redwood to cover under a BAA includes chat transcripts and clinician notes (yes/no).
2) If yes, can you share the vendor security questionnaire (or a link) — we’ll populate initial responses and return within 2 business days.
3) Ben / Karthik will follow up with technical details (KMS, audit logs, retention SLAs) and an estimated timeline for Dedicated onboarding.

Estimated timelines (rough): Dedicated setup + isolation: ~6–8 weeks after contract & infra prep. Private (VPC) lead time depends on networking schedule — plan for 4–10 weeks.

Happy to jump on a short technical call next week with your security engineer — suggest Tue/Wed.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: BAA_Draft_Redwood.docx (DOCX, draft BAA)

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PHI handling: BAA availability and deployment paths

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: chat transcripts and clinician-uploaded attachments will be in-scope as PHI.
- Questions for your tech team:
  1) Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest in Dedicated deployments?
  2) Can audit logs (full request/response metadata, with redacted token content) be forwarded to our Splunk instance?
  3) Do you have an SLA / evidence package for SOC 2 Type II we can include with procurement?

Also — for procurement planning: we prefer an AWS-hosted Dedicated pool in us-west-2. What is the earliest slot you typically have for provisioning? We have an internal go/no-go review in mid-April.

If you can ship a completed vendor questionnaire (we’ll share) plus a draft BAA, that would speed the procurement review.

Thanks,

Laurie Martin
Director, Security & Compliance | MedSecure Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PHI handling: BAA availability and deployment paths

Ben / Eve —

Short answers and artifacts:
1) KMS / customer-managed keys: supported for Private deployments by default. For Dedicated in major cloud providers (AWS us-west-2) we support customer KMS in most enterprise contracts; technically this is done via a dedicated key policy and optional HSM-backed CMKs. I attached implementation notes.
2) Audit logs: we can forward structured request/response metadata (headers, timestamps, model/version, token counts) to a customer endpoint (Splunk/CloudWatch) excluding protected token content by default; retention windows are configurable (30/90/365 days).
3) SOC 2: we maintain a SOC 2 Type II report; the summary deck is attached (Redwood_SOC2_Summary_2026.pdf). We’ll provide the redacted report under NDA if procurement requires the full artifact.
4) Provisioning timeline: if contract and networking approvals land quickly, we can schedule Dedicated provisioning in us-west-2 in ~6 weeks (target mid-May). If you need an accelerated slot we can attempt a 4-week expedited path but it requires prioritized engineering time and a signed SOW.

Next tacticals:
- Eve: please share the vendor security questionnaire link when you get it from MedSecure and I’ll start filling answers.
- Ben: propose a short tech Q&A with MedSecure’s security engineer (30 minutes) — I’m available Thu/Fri this week.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0334
